    Proposition 2.10(2): A₀ is representation-finite #

    prop:projective-evaluation(2): evaluation add C → mod A₀ is an equivalence, so the indecomposable A₀-modules are the evaluations of the finitely many objects of C.

    Every finite-dimensional module is the evaluation of a family (InjData.essSurj); an indecomposable one has local endomorphism ring and is a retract of one summand (exchange), which is an evaluation R_x with local endomorphism ring C(x, x) (full faithfulness), hence isomorphic to it. Modules of Alg F₀ are that paper's right A₀-modules; they are transported to right modules of (Alg F₀)ᵒᵖ along R ≅ Rᵒᵖᵒᵖ.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
